newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy May car sales rise but orders slowing - CSP.
newsitem.headline: Italy May car sales rise but orders slowing - CSP.

text.p: Italian new car registrations may have posted a 43.2 percent jump year on year in May but a survey of dealers showed that new orders are slowing down, car sector research body CSP said.

CSP said in its latest monthly report that the percentage of car dealers polled declaring a high level of orders fell in May to 40 percent from 52 percent in April, 64 percent in March and 87 percent in February.
The trend was even clearer when looking at forecasts for coming months, with only 22 percent of dealers seeing a rise in sales against 80 percent in February.
The government's cash incentive scheme for motorists to turn in old cars for scrapping in exchange for buying new models which was introduced in January is due to end in September.

"It looks even more probable that when the incentive scheme ends in September the market will not find any basis in the economy to result in a return of demand showing normal growth levels," CSP said.

Analysts noted that in France car sales have fallen consistently in the first four months of this year as weak demand persisted more than six months after the end of a similar car-buying incentive programme.
